# Thermomachines Thermomachines are devices that change the temperature of gases inside a [textlink="pipe network" link="PipeNetworks"] or in the surrounding atmosphere.
They are essential for maintaining gas temperatures in a variety of applications.
All thermomachines use [textlink="electric power" link="Power"] to heat or cool the atmosphere. The amount of heating or cooling they provide is directly related to how much power they consume.
Thermomachines also have an efficiency coefficient that determines how much they can heat or cool the atmosphere per unit of energy consumed.
To avoid overshooting the target, thermomachines reduce their heating or cooling power as they approach the target temperature. However, they still consume the same amount of electricity even while idle.
All thermomachines have a target-temperature tolerance of [color=orange][protodata="GasThermoMachineFreezer" comp="GasThermoMachine" member="TemperatureTolerance"/] K[/color]. This means they stop heating or cooling when the temperature is within [color=orange][protodata="GasThermoMachineFreezer" comp="GasThermoMachine" member="TemperatureTolerance"/] K[/color] of the target.
## Space Heater The space heater is a portable temperature-control device that heats or cools gas in the surrounding atmosphere. It is a simple and effective way to maintain a room's temperature without building a pipenet or another system.
They can often be found in Atmospherics, though the corresponding machine board can be printed at a circuit imprinter, usually located in Science.
The space heater can cool down to [color=orange][protodata="SpaceHeater" comp="SpaceHeater" member="MinTemperature"/] K[/color] and heat up to [color=orange][protodata="SpaceHeater" comp="SpaceHeater" member="MaxTemperature"/] K[/color].
It also has three power levels that determine how quickly it heats or cools the atmosphere.
Botany or Science will often request these devices to maintain the temperature of plants or their department.
## Pipenet Thermomachines (Freezer and Heater) Pipenet thermomachines are more powerful, stationary temperature-control devices that can heat or cool gas in a [textlink="pipenet" link="PipeNetworks"].
They consume [color=orange][protodata="GasThermoMachineFreezer" comp="GasThermoMachine" member="HeatCapacity" format="N0"/] W[/color] of power and can heat or cool gas in the pipenet to a maximum of [color=orange][protodata="GasThermoMachineFreezer" comp="GasThermoMachine" member="MaxTemperature"/] K[/color] or a minimum of [color=orange][protodata="GasThermoMachineFreezer" comp="GasThermoMachine" member="MinTemperature"/] K[/color].
You can change a thermomachine's mode by disassembling it and using a screwdriver on its machine board. The board can be printed at a circuit imprinter, usually located in Science.
## Hellfire Thermomachines Science can research more powerful thermomachines, aptly named hellfire heaters and freezers. These machines are much more powerful than their standard counterparts, but they also consume more power.
These machines consume [color=orange][protodata="GasThermoMachineHellfireFreezer" comp="GasThermoMachine" member="HeatCapacity" format="N0"/] W[/color] of power and can heat or cool gas in the pipenet to a maximum of [color=orange][protodata="GasThermoMachineHellfireFreezer" comp="GasThermoMachine" member="MaxTemperature"/] K[/color] or a minimum of [color=orange][protodata="GasThermoMachineHellfireFreezer" comp="GasThermoMachine" member="MinTemperature"/] K[/color].
However, they also leak [color=orange][protodata="GasThermoMachineHellfireFreezer" comp="GasThermoMachine" member="EnergyLeakPercentage" format="P0"/][/color] of their energy into the surroundings, heating or cooling the surrounding atmosphere accordingly. This can be dangerous without proper control.
